stepsTitle: How it works: convert Excel to CSV

steps.title: Drop your Excel file
steps.text: Drop an .xlsx, .xls, .xlsm or .ods file on this page or choose it. It is read in your browser and never uploaded.

steps.title: It opens as a CSV
steps.text: The first sheet is converted at once and opens in the CSV viewer, with commas between the columns and Arabic text kept intact.

steps.title: Check and edit it
steps.text: Search, sort, filter and edit the rows in the CSV viewer, so the CSV holds exactly what you need.

steps.title: Download
steps.text: Download saves the CSV. For a semicolon, tab or pipe instead of a comma, choose Download options in the More menu.

handlesTitle: What the Excel to CSV converter handles
handles: Values: each cell as its number format shows it, so dates, percentages and currencies keep their format, and formulas give their saved result. A number in the General format is written in full, so 123456789012 stays 123456789012 and long decimals keep their digits, up to the 15 significant digits Excel stores.
Sheets: the first sheet; for another, open the workbook in the Excel viewer, pick the sheet and use Convert.
Encoding: UTF-8, with the byte order mark Excel needs for Arabic and other non-Latin text whenever the sheet has any.
Delimiters: a comma, or a semicolon, tab or pipe from the CSV viewer's Download options.
limits: CSV holds values only: formulas, formatting, charts and images are not kept.
One sheet becomes one CSV; to save every sheet as its own CSV, use Split, merge and export sheets in the Excel viewer.
faqTitle: Excel to CSV: questions and answers

faq.question: How do I convert an Excel file with several sheets to CSV?
faq.answer: OpenAnyDoc's Excel to CSV converter takes the first sheet of the workbook. For another sheet, open the workbook in the Excel viewer, click the sheet's tab, then click Convert at the top and choose Convert to CSV: the sheet on screen opens as a CSV.

faq.question: Why does Arabic text look broken when I open the CSV in Excel?
faq.answer: Excel opens a UTF-8 CSV normally only if it was saved with a byte order mark. The CSV made here gets that mark whenever the sheet has Arabic or other non-Latin text, so Excel shows it correctly. If a CSV already shows broken Arabic, see Fix broken Arabic in a CSV.

link.text: Fix broken Arabic in a CSV

faq.question: Can I use a semicolon instead of a comma?
faq.answer: Yes. The CSV opens in the CSV viewer: choose Download options in the More menu and pick a semicolon, tab or pipe. A semicolon suits Excel in regions that write decimals with a comma, where a comma-separated file lands in one column. If that happens, see CSV opens in one column.

faq.question: Are formulas kept in the CSV?
faq.answer: No. CSV holds text only, so each formula is written as the result saved in the workbook. Keep the Excel file if you still need the formulas.

faq.question: Are dates and numbers written the way Excel shows them?
faq.answer: Yes. Each cell is written as the text its number format gives, so a date keeps its date format and a price keeps its currency sign, instead of becoming the number Excel stores behind it. A number in the General format is written in full, even when a narrow column shows it as 1.23457E+11, so 123456789012 stays 123456789012.

faq.question: Is my workbook uploaded to convert it?
faq.answer: No. The workbook is read and converted by your browser on your device; nothing is sent to a server.

faq.question: How do I convert XLSX to CSV without Excel?
faq.answer: Open the .xlsx, .xls, .xlsm or .ods file in a browser-based converter such as OpenAnyDoc and download the CSV: the first sheet is written with commas between the columns and Arabic text intact. Nothing is uploaded and no copy of Excel is needed. To only read the workbook, see how to open an XLSX file without Excel.
